name: Bentley Systems, Incorporated

profile.description: Bentley Systems provides infrastructure engineering software — design, simulation, construction and asset-operations applications (MicroStation, OpenRoads, SYNCHRO, the iTwin digital-twin platform and Cesium geospatial 3D) — sold mostly on subscription to civil, structural, utility and industrial engineering firms and owner-operators. FY2025 revenue was $1.50B (+11%) with net income of $278M [3]. Q2 2026 revenue rose 12.8% to $410.7M, ARR reached $1.536B (12% constant-currency growth) and net revenue retention was 109% [1]. Nicholas Cumins became CEO in July 2024, the first non-Bentley-family CEO in the company's 40-year history [4].

innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Bentley has moved from perpetual licenses to an ARR model ($1.536B ARR, 92% of Q2 2026 revenue from subscriptions of $378.6M) and built the iTwin digital-twin platform and Cesium 3D geospatial layer into a cloud infrastructure stack, opening owner-operator and asset-lifecycle revenue beyond design seats [1][3]. Revenue compounded from $801.5M (2020) to $1.50B (2025) [3]. AI Deployment (1/2): Leadership is explicitly reorganizing go-to-market around AI adoption — Andy Rahden was promoted to Chief Revenue Officer to expand AI adoption, with Cumins stressing a fast feedback loop to product teams — but no quantified AI revenue or savings was found [4]. Market Share (1/2): A leading infrastructure-engineering software vendor alongside Autodesk with 109% net retention, but no category share data was found [1]. Pipeline (1/2): AI embedded in existing workflows is the stated roadmap, without dated next-gen launches or revenue targets [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D of $307.6M is 20.5% of FY2025 revenue — solid, but at or below design-software peers rather than top quartile [3].
innovation.label: DEVELOPING

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Bentley's stated purpose — software to advance infrastructure for better quality of life and sustainable growth — ties its products to the roads, water, power and rail that society depends on, and 40 years as a founder-family company gave it a distinctive engineering ethos that the new CEO publicly pledged to preserve [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No specific charitable program with dollar amounts was identified in research; ESG materials focus on the sustainability outcomes of customers' projects rather than direct giving [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found, and recent employee commentary cites substantial layoffs and dissolved teams during the post-family transition [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of net insider buying in the last 12 months.
inspiration.label: WEAK

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on Growth metrics (10 weight units): weighted sum 9.01 / 10 → 9. ROE of 24.5% (2x) and 5-year revenue CAGR of 13.4% (2x; derived from FMP revenue of $801.5M in 2020 and $1.50B in 2025) both max out, as do revenue growth of 12.8% YoY [2][3]. Profit margin of 18.1% scores 0.91, Forward P/E of 26.9 scores 0.83, and D/E of 105% scores 0.85 [2]. Forward PEG of 1.57 (Yahoo Finance reported) scores 0.72 on its 2x weight — the main drag. Liquidity is ample: ~2.5M shares/day × $42.40 ≈ $107M daily dollar volume [2].
infrastructure.label: STRONG

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Bentley's applications are the engineering system of record for regulated, liability-bearing infrastructure design — code-compliant structural, road and utility models plus digital twins of operating assets — which creates switching costs and data moats that generic AI tools cannot easily replicate [1][4]. Management frames AI as something to be embedded in the workflows where engineers already design and operate assets, not a standalone product, and 109% net retention shows customers are not churning [1][4]. It scores below 'immune' because AI-driven design automation could reduce the number of engineering seats and pressure per-user pricing, and the stock has de-rated on that concern. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI revenue was disclosed.
ai_resilience.label: MODERATE

infinite_game.summary: Bentley was built over four decades by a founding family around a durable cause — better infrastructure for society — and it has shown flexibility by moving to subscriptions, cloud and open digital-twin standards. The first non-family CEO is now testing whether that cause survives a more commercial, AI-driven reorganization, and layoffs have strained the trust that the family era built.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Advancing infrastructure for quality of life and sustainable growth is a service-oriented, idealistic cause that has guided product investment for 40 years under the Bentley brothers [4]. It earns less than 3 because it has not yet been proven through the leadership transition to Nicholas Cumins in July 2024 [4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The founding family handed the CEO role to an outsider-to-the-family executive and committed to preserving the engineering ethos, and the company accepted the near-term revenue drag of shifting to subscription/E365 consumption models for long-term durability [1][4]. There is not yet a pattern of multiple costly bets under the new CEO.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Long family stewardship created stability, but recent employee commentary describes chaotic change management, substantial layoffs and dissolved teams during the AI-focused reorganization, alongside others praising culture and work-life balance [4]. Mixed evidence lands at adequate trust.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Bentley moved from perpetual licenses to subscriptions, from desktop to cloud, and from design tools to iTwin/Cesium digital twins of operating assets [1][3]. These are meaningful but incremental evolutions of the same engineering-software franchise rather than a reinvention.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Bentley's open-ecosystem strategy — open-sourcing the iTwin.js platform and acquiring Cesium, whose open 3D Tiles standard is used across the industry — reflects a mindset of raising the whole field and interoperating with competitors rather than locking them out [3].

investment_thesis: Bentley is a high-quality compounding software franchise: revenue grew from $801.5M in 2020 to $1.50B in 2025 (13.4% CAGR) and Q2 2026 revenue rose 12.8% to $410.7M with ARR of $1.536B growing 12% in constant currency and 109% net retention [1][3]. ROE of 24.5% and an 18.1% net margin show real operating leverage, free cash flow rose to $63.8M in Q2, and management reiterated 2026 guidance of 10.5–12.5% constant-currency ARR growth and $1.69–1.72B revenue [1][2]. Global infrastructure spending on grids, water and transport — partly driven by AI data-center power needs — is a multi-year tailwind for its engineering and digital-twin tools.
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and AI seat risk. At 45x trailing and 26.9x forward earnings with a 1.57 PEG, the stock prices in steady double-digit growth, and Q2 operating margin slipped to 21.6% from 23.2% while revenue came in slightly below consensus [1][2]. If generative design automation reduces the number of engineers per project, per-seat economics could compress before consumption pricing offsets it. The leadership transition and layoffs add execution risk, and D/E of 105% is higher than typical for software [2][4]. Inspire Impact Score of 69 (ALIGNED).
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (early November) — consensus revenue of $420.4M and non-GAAP EPS of $0.32; confirming ARR growth at the upper half of the 10.5–12.5% range would ease AI-disruption fears [1]
Monetization of AI inside existing workflows under new CRO Andy Rahden, converting AI adoption into consumption-based ARR [4]
Grid, water and transport spending tied to data-center power demand and public infrastructure programs expanding the user base for OpenRoads, SYNCHRO and iTwin [1]
key_risks: Generative design automation reducing engineering headcount at customers, compressing seat-based subscription revenue
Operating margin compression (21.6% vs 23.2% in Q2) if AI investment and go-to-market reorganization costs outpace revenue growth [1]
Cultural disruption after the first non-family CEO transition, with reported layoffs and team dissolutions risking loss of key engineering talent [4]
